Choose between competing SITAR specifications with a written rule

Source: R/curve-sitar.R
wgh_sitar_select.Rd

Fits the candidate specifications and applies the selection rule of Ho et al. (2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358986): a model is acceptable only if it converged, its mean velocity stays above velocity_tol in the late-adolescent tail, its random effects are identifiable and its residual error is no more than twice that of the best candidate. The first acceptable candidate is kept unless a more complex candidate fitted to the same age window (BIC is not comparable across windows) improves BIC by more than bic_margin while leaving APHV and PHV stable. The reason for the choice is returned.

Usage

wgh_sitar_select(
  x,
  candidates = list(F1 = list(df = 4, fixed = "a + b + c", random = "a + b + c",
    age_range = c(6, 16)), F2 = list(df = 4, fixed = "a + b + c", random = "a + b + c",
    age_range = c(6, 15)), F3 = list(df = 4, fixed = "a + b + c + d", random =
    "a + b + c + d", age_range = c(6, 16))),
  velocity_tol = 0,
  bic_margin = 10,
  aphv_tol = 0.3,
  phv_tol = 0.5
)

Arguments

x

Growth data for one sex.

candidates

Named list of argument lists for wgh_fit_sitar(), ordered from simplest to most complex.

velocity_tol

Minimum acceptable tail velocity (cm/year).

bic_margin

BIC improvement required to prefer a more complex model.

aphv_tol, phv_tol

Stability tolerances relative to the first model.

Value

An object of class wgh_sitar_selection with fits, table (diagnostics, the criteria and why_not, the reasons a candidate was not acceptable), selected (name) and reason.

Examples

# \donttest{
boys <- growdat2_mini[growdat2_mini$sex == "Male", ]
sel <- wgh_sitar_select(boys, candidates = list(
  F1 = list(df = 4, fixed = "a + b + c", random = "a + b + c", age_range = c(6, 18)),
  F2 = list(df = 5, fixed = "a + b + c", random = "a + b + c", age_range = c(6, 18))))
sel$table
#> # A tibble: 2 × 21
#>   model converged n_children   AIC   BIC sigma  RMSE  sd_a  sd_b   sd_c  sd_d
#>   <chr> <lgl>          <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 F1    TRUE             418 6198. 6274. 0.535 0.372  3.89 0.526 0.0670    NA
#> 2 F2    TRUE             418 6218. 6299. 0.533 0.368  3.98 0.491 0.0658    NA
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: min_velocity_tail <dbl>, max_re_corr <dbl>, APHV <dbl>,
#> #   PHV <dbl>, identifiable <lgl>, plausible_tail <lgl>, good_fit <lgl>,
